description: The bar chart illustrates the “effect” scores—likely representing model performance or probing accuracy—of four multilingual BERT variants (mBERT-B₂, XLM-B₂, XLM-R₂, and mBERT-B₂ again, though likely a typo and meant to be distinct; legend shows mBERT-B₂, XLM-B₂, XLM-R₂, and possibly another variant) across various language families and isolates, as part of a morphosyntactic probing study. The vertical axis, labeled “effect,” ranges from 0 to approximately 35, with major gridlines at intervals of 10. The horizontal axis lists language groupings: IE-Romance, IE-Slavic family, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. Each group contains four colored bars corresponding to the models: light green (mBERT-B₂), dark green (XLM-R₂), light red (mBERT-B₂ again, possibly mislabeled), and dark red (XLM-B₂). Error bars extend vertically from each bar, indicating variability or confidence intervals. In most categories, XLM-B₂ (dark red) and XLM-R₂ (dark green) show higher effect scores than mBERT variants, with XLM-B₂ often peaking in Semitic and Uralic. The Semitic group shows the highest overall scores, particularly for XLM-B₂ (~35), while Uralic shows the lowest, with all models scoring below 10. The chart is tilted diagonally, and the legend is positioned in the upper right, with color-coded model names. No bars are shaded or emphasized beyond their color coding, and the bars are not sorted by height within groups.
